coaching.title: Hills 6 mi + 1,200 ft — Descending Focus
coaching.message: Peak phase, 45 days out. Today is your first dedicated vert session: 6 mi with ~1,200 ft on the San Salvador terrain. Climb easy to steady, letting HR touch Zone 3 (up toward 155-165 bpm) only on the steepest pitches — power hike anything that spikes you above that. The real work is the descents: relaxed upright posture, quick light feet, controlled eccentric braking. Julian Alps has ~2,500m of alpine vert and the downhills wreck quads that aren't trained, so treat every descent as a rep. Go at first light for the heat. If resting HR was above 65 or you feel flat, cut to 4 mi easy — no ego.

coaching.title: Fuel the Vert
coaching.message: Short session but heat-heavy in El Salvador. Pre-run: a small carb hit (banana or a gel, ~30g) plus 300-400ml with sodium. It's under an hour so you don't need mid-run fuel, but carry fluid with electrolytes and sip on the climbs. Post-run, hit your recovery window within 30 min: 25-30g protein plus carbs to reload. Descending is eccentric-heavy and tears muscle, so protein today matters as much as the run itself.

coaching.title: Protect the Quads
coaching.message: Eccentric braking on descents = delayed soreness 24-48h out. Get ahead of it: 10 min of easy walking to flush the legs, then foam roll quads, calves, and IT band tonight. Elevate the legs for a bit and prioritize sleep — you're in peak volume now and adaptation is happening between sessions, not during them.

coaching.title: Own the Downhills
coaching.message: Most runners survive climbs and fear descents — flip that. Every controlled downhill today is free time you'll bank at the Julian Alps. Six weeks out, this is where races are won: not on the up, but on relaxed, confident, quick-footed descending. Practice it now so it's automatic on race day.
